Reading Order Prediction as Relation Extraction We test the proposed baseline model with word-level and segment-level reading order prediction tasks of ROOR. We take the ISDR annotations as the segment-level labels, and utilize the arranged words within segments together with the segment-level annotations to generate word-level labels. We adopt LayoutLMv3-base/large (Huang et al., 2022) as the backbone text-and-Layout encoder for the proposed ROP model. In evaluation, we follow the train/validation split from EC-FUNSD and models are evaluated by F1 score. Enhancing Downstream VrD Tasks with Reading Order Relation To examine the effectiveness of reading order relation information in enhancing downstream VrD tasks, we enhance pre-trained text-and-query models (PTLMs) with additional reading order inputs. Two baseline models are examined: LayoutLMv3 as the most popular PTLM, and GeoLayoutLM (Luo et al., 2023) as a representative relation-aware PTLM. We assess the baseline models and their reading-order-relation-enhanced (RORE) variants on semantic entity recognition (SER) and entity linking (EL) of EC-FUNSD, leveraging the ground truth reading order information in the ROOR dataset. Quality of Pseudo Reading Order Relation Labels for Downstream Tasks Enhancing an arbitrary VrD task with additional reading order Table 2: Performance of LayoutLMv3 and GeoLayoutLM and their corresponding RORE methods on ECFUNSD. Reproduced results are marked with * (see Appendix D).

relation inputs is expected. However, it is impractical to manually annotate each sample with such information. Consequently, a robust off-the-shelf ROP model is expected to generalize well to any target domain and generate high-quality pseudo reading order relation labels for unseen datasets, since VrDs in real application could cover various domains and have high diversity in layouts. To validate the effectiveness of the generated pseudo labels, we conduct experiments on VrD-IE/QA tasks with utilizing the pseudo reading order information generated by an off-the-shelf LayoutLMv3-large model solely trained on the ROOR dataset. For IE, we adopt three popular benchmarks for SER and EL: FUNSD (Jaume et al., 2019), CORD (Park et al., 2019) and SROIE (Huang et al., 2019). For QA, we choose four popular benchmarks that primarily featuring on layout understanding and IE, but not commonsense or complex reasoning which are less relevant to layout understanding: DocVQA (Mathew et al., 2021), InfoVQA (Mathew et al., 2022), WTQ (Borchmann et al., 2021) and TextVQA (Singh et al., 2019). A generative variant of LayoutLMv3 with a BART decoder (Lewis et al., 2019) is used as the baseline model, the performance of which is evaluated by average normalized Levenshtein similarity (ANLS). We report the performance of baseline and RORE models on these datasets. The implementation details of the above experiments are illustrated in Appendix D.

Reading Order Prediction Methods For training the baseline sequence-based ROP methods (LR and TPP) on ROOR, these models are supervised by the topology-sorted sequence of the original label for each sample. The training process Table 5: Performance of LLM-based generative methods and our methods on three VrD-SER benchmarks.
Method#ParamsFUNSDCORDSROIE

LayoutLLM (2024)7B79.9863.1072.12

generally follows the settings reported in the original papers, with the only exception that we fine-tune each model by 500 epochs. During inference, these models produce word sequences as outputs, and each two adjacent words are extracted as a predicted reading order relation pair. In segment-level evaluation of these models, we order the segments according to the first appearance of their words in the original outputs, constructing segment sequences as outputs. The proposed relation-extraction-based ROP model adopts LayoutLMv3-base (Huang et al., 2022) and LayoutMask (Tu et al., 2023) as the backbones. The maximum sequence length of textual tokens for both of them is 2048. The maximum layout elements is set to 512 for word-level task and 256 for segment-level task, ensuring the number of layout elements within each ROOR samples should not exceeds the maximum. The head size of the global pointer decoding network (i.e. the dimension of query and key vectors in Eqn. 3) is set to 128. We use an AdamW optimizer with $5\%$ linear warming-up steps, a 0.1 dropout rate, and a 1e-5 weight decay, together with a cosine scheduler. The learning rate is searched from $\{1\mathrm{e} - 5,2\mathrm{e} - 5,5\mathrm{e} - 5,1\mathrm{e} - 4,1.5\mathrm{e} - 4,2\mathrm{e} - 4\}$ for LayoutLMv3-base and $\{1\mathrm{e} - 5,2\mathrm{e} - 5,5\mathrm{e} - 5,1\mathrm{e} - 4\}$ for LayoutLMv3-large, and the best learning rate is $1\mathrm{e} - 4 / 2\mathrm{e} - 5$ , respectively. We fine-tune the model by 1,000 epochs (10,000 steps) on 1 A800 GPUs with batch size being 16 and patience being 50 for early stopping. Reading Order Relation Enhanced Methods for Downstream VrD Tasks For information extraction tasks, the enhanced semantic entity recognition (SER) and entity linking (EL) models strictly keep the same settings of the original implementation (Zhang et al., 2024), with all experiments using the learning rate of 1e-5, batch size of 16, number of fine-tuning epochs of 500 and early stopping patience of 50. The initial value for $\lambda^l$ is all set to 10 in all layers, and the learning rate of the $\lambda$ s are searched between the original learning rate and 1e-2, where the Table 6: Ablation study on the level of bounding box information used in the baseline ROP model.
Task LevelMethodBounding Box Level
WordSegment
WordLayoutLMv3-base90.2687.93
LayoutLMv3-large93.0192.80
SegmentLayoutLMv3-base63.0068.60
LayoutLMv3-large76.0482.38
latter is for faster convergence. Specially, in these three groups of experiment: LayoutLMv3-base-FUNSD-SER, GeoLayoutLM-FUNSD-SER and GeoLayoutLM-FUNSD-EL, since we used the fine-tuned weights provided by the official repositories of LayoutLMv3 $^2$ and GeoLayoutLM $^3$ which are fairly close to the optimal state, we only use the reading order information in the first 4 layers, and the value for $\lambda^l, 1 \leq l \leq 4$ are set to 0.1 initially. In Tab. 2 and 3, for the baseline models, we report the bias-removed running results from (Zhang et al., 2024) together with our running results using its implementation. Among other baseline methods, the performance of GraphLayoutLM (Li et al., 2023) can only be reproduced on CORD according to its official release $^4$ . We are unable to reproduce its performance on other datasets since the pre-trained weights are not released. Therefore, we only report its performance on CORD from its official release. These reproduced results are marked with $*$ . For generative VrD-QA tasks, the baseline model is comprised of a LayoutLMv3-base encoder and a BART-base decoder (Lewis et al., 2019), and is pre-trained on open-sourced VrD-QA-form data filtered from InstructDoc (Tanaka et al., 2024) for better initialization. The model is then fine-tuned on each dataset using learning rate of 1e-5, batch size of 48, with an AdamW optimizer with $2\%$ linear warming-up steps and a cosine scheduler for 6 epochs. For the RORE settings, the reading-orderrelation-aware attention module is only applied to its decoder, and the other settings keep the same of RORE-VrD-IE experiments.
